analysis.title: Paul Donovan's daily audio: The triumph of the optimists
key_insights: Market optimism revived on news that the Iranian government has been granted powers to negotiate with the US.
Reports of limited US attacks on Iran overnight did not dent the optimism. Investors appear willing to reduce the oil risk premium, but supply and demand fundamentals have not changed.
There is a floor under oil prices as long as the price mechanism is still needed to ration supply.
The US midterms complicate talks, but a US effort to address the affordability crisis seems warranted if some in the administration want post-2028 political careers.
The RBA raised rates by a quarter point, as expected, with dovish overtones.
Several ECB speakers are scheduled, but none appear to be front-runners to succeed Lagarde as ECB president.
US labor market data due is described as lacking reliability and credibility, including job openings figures. Durable and capital goods orders are also due, and much of the AI story is imported.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The hike was expected and came with dovish overtones, so it signals limited further tightening.
Release is due, but UBS says the labor data lacks reliability and credibility, so it carries little signal.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Release is due. UBS notes much of the AI investment story is imported, so US orders may capture only part of it.
